evidence: In this experiment set, our BERT implementation is compared to several systems that participated in the MEDDOCAN challenge: a CRF classifier BIBREF18, a spaCy entity recogniser BIBREF18, and NLNDE BIBREF12, the winner of the shared task and current state of the art for sensitive information detection and classification in Spanish clinical text. Specifically, we include the results of a domain-independent NLNDE model (S2), and the results of a model enriched with domain-specific embeddings (S3). title: Sensitive Data Detection and Classification in Spanish Clinical Text: Experiments with BERT
answer_short: BERT remains only 0.3 F1-score points behind the winner in MEDDOCAN and would have achieved second place. With 1% of the dataset, BERT suffers only a 7-point F1-score loss, outperforming other models.
answer_rationale: Text 5 states that BERT is 0.3 F1-score points behind the MEDDOCAN winner and would have achieved second place. Text 6 and Text 7 indicate that BERT is the most robust to training-data reduction, suffering only a 7-point F1-score loss with 1% of the dataset, outperforming CRF and spaCy models which lose 32 and 39 points respectively. Text 10 adds that BERT's F1-score is 1.9 points higher than the next most competitive result, with 5 points higher recall.
